relations.subject: clusters:storage-auto-expansion
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - this page's own dedicated Storage Auto-Expansion section is the clearest single-page statement of the AWS/GCP-vs-Azure difference found so far in the registry
relations.evidence: When your usage exceeds 75% on Azure clusters, Capella doubles the current storage capacity. Storage increases for Azure use the replacement and rebalancing of nodes, which can affect performance until the process completes.

relations.subject: clusters:storage-auto-expansion
relations.evidence: When your usage exceeds 75% on AWS and GCP clusters, Capella triggers a 50% increase in the current storage capacity. Storage increases are in place without any data movement or performance impact.

relations.subject: clusters:storage-auto-expansion
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - a second, distinct AWS-specific behavior (a rate limit, not the data-movement difference)
relations.evidence: AWS clusters can only auto-expand storage once every 6 hours.

relations.subject: clusters:storage-auto-expansion
relations.evidence: When deploying a new cluster with AWS or GCP, storage auto-expansion is always on, and you cannot turn it off. Clusters deploying with Azure have auto-expansion off by default with the option to turn it on.

notable_absence.finding: This page is entirely about scaling dimensions (nodes, instance size, whole Services) and storage auto-expansion, yet never mentions storage engine even though storage-engine choice would plausibly affect scaling/resident-ratio guardrails (databases.md's guardrail table keys thresholds by Couchstore vs Magma). Consistent with the databases.json/create-database.json finding that storage engine isn't part of the cluster-level configuration surface this batch's pages document.

cross_component_finding: The Cluster Scaling Statuses list here (19 values) is a strict superset of the 4-value status table on off-on-database.md (OFF, Turning Off, Turning On, Healthy) - off-on-database.md's table is a legitimate UI-scoped subset (only the statuses relevant to the on/off toggle), not an inconsistency, but the reconciler should model clusters:cluster-status as one enum with off-on-database.md's table as a partial view, not mint a second status concept.
